why_this_file_exists: The gate ratchet needs a list of unproven gates, each with a reason and a
slot. That list changes every time a gate closes — which made it a
recurring edit to tools/label_gates.py, and the repository's own churn
guard was right to object: a source file edited once per closed gate is a
file whose data does not belong in it.
So the backlog is data with ONE authority, and closing a gate edits this
file instead of the checker. The checker's logic stops changing entirely.

categories.blocked: something external prevents the attempt: a device, an arm64 host, an integration nobody has done yet.
categories.in_flight: the current run closes it. False the moment the run finishes, so entries must leave.
categories.measured_below: it WAS attempted and the number came up short. Added 2026-08-17, on Fable 5's adjudication, because the other two categories both lie about this state: in_flight implies pending work nobody owns, and blocked implies the attempt could not be made. The name is self-refuting against both misreadings — 'measured' rules out 'never attempted', 'below' rules out 'passed'. An empty slot is honest here; a fabricated owner is not.

measured_below.2c: score=1.097412  bar=1.107  delta=-0.009588  date=2026-08-17  prior=1.0996. Run on a clean brains directory over the recorded 39-run corpus; full report in docs/GATE_2C_REPLAY.md and tools/suite-logs/replay_2c_evolution.json. Nothing was re-run to chase the bar, nothing tuned, and the bar was not moved. The finding the run bought for free: of four components, `trend` sat at exactly 1.000 in every epoch while `atlas` carried the entire rise (1.000 -> 1.295) — an estimator that does not move across five epochs is where the headroom is. Slot: empty, deliberately. Three options are recorded in that document (the system improves, the bar is re-derived from its provenance, or the gate is re-scoped and dated as 2b was) and none is chosen, because none is the measurer's to choose.
